title: Are Economists Always More Introverted? Analyzing Consistency in Persona-Assigned LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Assigning professional personas (e.g., economist, pilot, nurse) to LLMs via system prompts and using an LLM-as-a-judge to measure unintended spillover effects into specific personality traits (e.g., economists acting introverted) across multiple tasks like essays, surveys, and chats.

Prompting LLMs with predefined political personas based on the Political Compass Test and evaluating their consistency, as well as observing the models' default ideological stances, using Shannon entropy across structured and open-ended text generation tasks.

Assigning emotional states (happy/sad) or Big Five personality traits as personas and evaluating whether the LLMs default to stereotypical associations (e.g., a 'sad' persona consistently being portrayed as introverted and less conscientious) across different response dimensions.

Observing the LLM's default tendency to output highly agreeable, open, and conscientious responses when specific antagonistic or unconscientious traits are not explicitly assigned, utilizing an LLM-as-a-judge to classify default trait manifestations.
